answer: Behavioral Correlation Audit. After the fact, cluster agent accounts by reuse of rare action sequences—unusual timing offsets, shared counterparties, near-identical transaction orderings—flagging a meadow of accounts whose cross-correlation exceeds chance. Each identity must clear a per-account audit cost: sustained activity history whose statistical ripple is expensive to fabricate independently. A flagged sybil cluster loses its quill of accumulated reputation and all queued payouts, so every fake identity costs real compute plus forfeited earnings.
